rows.fact: The programme face strength is 345 MPa. A partial SAE AMS 7902 extract gives a minimum tensile yield of 206.8 MPa. The strength index of the specification floor is worse than the programme tuple.
NTRS 19940006718 cites Fenn 1967 compression strengths for SR-200 sheet. The extract used here stopped before those numbers. They were not invented.

No published yearly area of SR-200 sheet was found. USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026 gives about 230 t US apparent consumption of beryllium in 2025. That is not sheet area, and most of it is not unalloyed sheet.
AlBeMet AM162 rolled-sheet gauge and yearly area were not on the pages read.

The Vasiliev extract prints quasi-isotropic specific modulus as 3530 and 3820. Those figures are read here as thousands of metres. Read as bare metres, the densities are not composites and the rows would be dropped.
The M60J composite density uses an assumed epoxy density of 1200 kg/m3. The Toray sheet states fiber density and 60 percent fiber volume, not the cured-laminate density.
No measured quasi-isotropic compressive modulus was found for M60J or for the CNT yarn laminate. The unidirectional rows are upper bounds, not the membrane.
A secondary table of Miralon sheet mixed modulus and strength. Modulus was not used.
No measured graphene sheet, in a gauge and area a face could use, was opened. A theoretical monolayer modulus is not a product.
No ceramic-film datasheet other than CVD diamond was opened.
Ultracor UCF-51 published ribbon shear and compressive strength. Through-thickness modulus was not on the sheet read, so its wrinkling support is unranked.
The HexWeb CR-III 5056 table that was read has no grade below 1.0 pcf. A lighter aluminium honeycomb was not shown.
AF 163-2U at 0.015 lb/ft2 is a catalog weight. Flatwise strength at that weight was not in the rows read, and no row was on beryllium faces.
066 decides which face index governs. This card ranks all three and does not wait for that card.
Face area counts both skins at the outer radius. The inner skin is smaller.
The diamond strength used is tensile at 500 µm. Compression of a window was not the number on the Diamond Materials page.
10.2514/3.5568 and 10.2514/3.1932 were not opened and are not quoted. They are not material-property sources for this card.
